paper_title: Leveraging Reasoning Model Answers to Enhance Non-Reasoning Model   Capability
caption: Category Distribution of dataset
model_annotation: The pie chart illustrates the category distribution of a dataset, segmented into six distinct categories: “chat,” “math,” “tooluse,” “multi turn chat,” “code,” and “instruction follow.” The largest segment is “chat,” accounting for 41.2% of the total (546,526 instances), followed by “math” at 21.9% (290,496 instances). “Tooluse” comprises 11.6% (154,358 instances), while “multi turn chat” represents 9.3% (123,615 instances). “Code” makes up 9.0% (119,563 instances), and the smallest segment is “instruction follow” at 6.9% (91,460 instances). Each category is color-coded and labeled with both its percentage and absolute count, with a corresponding legend in the upper left corner for reference. The segments are arranged clockwise starting from the top-right, with “chat” occupying the largest wedge in light red, followed by “math” in blue, “tooluse” in green, “multi turn chat” in orange, “code” in lavender, and “instruction follow” in pink.
